quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop and back up immediately.
Road and driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to exit the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road and driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn that work is happening on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to return to the main road after a stop, you must:
questions.explanation: You must yield to any transit vehicle returning to the main road after a stop. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely merge into traffic.

questions.question: Leaving the scene of a crash is:

options.text: The most efficient way to handle an accident.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to leave the scene of a crash that causes property damage, injury, or death. You must stay, share your information, and help if needed.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances to drivers.
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show directions and distances to specific places. They help drivers who are unfamiliar with the area.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Suggested driving speeds for the area
The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in poor conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum or minimum legal speed for the road. These limits are for good conditions. You must drive slower when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what other drivers are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow traffic light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: At a four-way stop:

options.text: The driver who arrives first goes first.
The driver who arrives last goes first.
One driver should wave others to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first goes first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, all drivers must stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Slow down to reduce the risk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming road hazards. This sign warns that traffic is coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before you move into the other lane, quickly look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver more room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver more room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This creates space in front of your vehicle, making it easier and safer for them to complete the pass.

questions.question: At an intersection with no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?

options.text: You are not required to stop.
Slow down to make sure the road is clear.
Stop where you can see 200 feet on each side, even if it means entering the intersection.
Stop where you have a clear view of traffic before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop where you have a clear view of traffic before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Stop at the closest point to the intersection where you can see oncoming traffic. Do not enter the intersection to get a better view.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate is lowered.
Ignore how many tracks there are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be prepared to stop for trains or other vehicles using the tracks.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you to possible trains. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends or road narrows ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends or road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on yellow background. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending or the road is narrowing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead will be divided. Keep to the right of the divider or median.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to tell drivers to let you through.
Drive around a car that blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When can you drive in a lane showing a red X signal?

options.text: If there is no oncoming traffic.
If you are passing the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: Lane signals show which lanes are open or closed. A red X means that lane is closed. Never drive in a lane under a red X signal.

questions.question: When railroad crossing signals are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for a train. Also watch for lowered crossing gates and listen for train sounds.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, always signal first, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: What do orange signs mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones on highways. These diamond-shaped signs have black letters or symbols and warn drivers that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is about to hit you?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when they may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: What happens to fines for traffic violations in construction zones?
questions.explanation: In Florida, fines are doubled for traffic violations in construction zones. You may also face penalties up to $1,000 and be required to take a driving school course.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: Solid white lines separate lanes going the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines also separate same-direction lanes and can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: Held safely by a strong adult.
Standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Safely because they are small and won't get hurt.
Never standing in the vehicle — always properly secured.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never standing in the vehicle — always properly secured.
questions.explanation: Children need special seats designed for their size. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always fasten children properly in a seat.

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs about upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs for hazards ahead are yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down after you enter the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same in the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic in the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you enter the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp. Then slow down safely.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to the one you were in. This is the safest way to turn.

questions.question: When it starts raining while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Rain reduces visibility and makes roads slippery. Slow down and turn on your headlights. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see, pull to the side of the road and stop until it improves.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you may stop only:

options.text: To avoid conflict with other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid conflict with other traffic.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic light, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and SUVs have large areas behind them that the driver cannot see in the mirrors.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the car radio before backing up to get the attention of anyone near you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: It is hard to see behind your vehicle. Always walk to the back and check for children and small objects before getting in and backing up.

questions.question: If a traffic light is not working, drivers should:

options.text: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
Treat the intersection as a roundabout.
Drive without stopping but proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is broken, treat it like a four-way stop. The driver who gets there first has the right-of-way.

questions.question: If an oncoming car is heading toward you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Blow your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Blow your horn, steer left, and brake.
Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in the center of your lane, blow your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, honk to get the driver's attention. If they do not move, steer to the right. Do not steer left because they might correct and you could still crash. Brake firmly to slow down and reduce impact damage.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This warning sign alerts you to a steep hill ahead. Adjust your speed to avoid damaging your brakes or having a crash.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Your brake lights show that you are slowing down or stopping. Always keep your brake lights working.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When you see a steady green light, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving unless there are cars or people already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving unless there are cars or people already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and cars in the intersection pass first. You can go, but drive slowly enough to stop if the light changes.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. Which lane should you be in?

options.text: The lane with the least traffic.

questions.explanation: When you turn left onto a one-way street, turn into the left lane. This is the lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen when you drink alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, makes it hard to see clearly, messes up your judgment of speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take risks. It does not help you concentrate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that right turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be treated as:

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
Good places to park your car.
A place where you must stop.

questions.explanation: Always treat railroad crossings as dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs and signals. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a car with airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a slow crash.
Make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce the chance of being hurt or killed. Children age 12 and under should sit in the back seat properly restrained. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat with an airbag.

questions.question: Which of these can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: What should you do if your right wheels leave the road?

options.text: Immediately pull all the way off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Release the gas pedal, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal, slow down, then ease back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Don't panic. Release the gas, keep both hands on the wheel, and steer straight. Slow down and gently steer back onto the road with a small turn. Check for traffic before getting back on the pavement.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Make your car need a tune-up sooner.

questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases and cools hot gases from the engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust can be very dangerous and can make you drowsy while driving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
Divided highway starts ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
Merge ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
Winding road ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to the safe speed shown.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves to the right and shows the safe speed to drive (in this case, 35 mph).
